text:
eli: Quick follow-up from the RBAC -> capability projection RFC. Main open concern: when we change the role->cap mapping, how do we ensure cache coherence in the data plane without mass invalidation causing spikes?

zoe: Good call-out. Two problems: 1) correctness (don't accidentally grant new caps early), 2) stability (don't thundering-herd fetch every mapping on rollout).

harper: Proposal: attach a small mapping_version to minted cap_tokens (and to role projection records). Data plane caches mapping blobs keyed by mapping_id+version. When we update a projection we increment version and publish a delta event. Runtimes see version mismatch and either fetch new blob lazily or consult a local denylist for newly added caps until blob is refreshed.

eli: How do we avoid accidental privilege gain during rollout if some services fetch quickly and others are slow?

zoe: Safety-first path: changes that *add* capabilities to a role are staged as follows: create new mapping_version in preview, run in audit/observe mode for X hours, then promote. During promote we tag tokens minted before promote as "legacy" and only tokens minted after promote get the new mapping_version. Runtimes that haven't refreshed still honor "legacy" tokens and deny the new caps because their token's mapping_version hasn't changed. So no early grant.

harper: For removal of caps we can be more aggressive: publish revoke hints that cause runtimes to consult control plane for the affected subjects (or use per-subject gen bump). Since removal reduces privilege, a short-lived mismatch is less risky but we must audit for denied calls.

eli: What about tokens already minted that reference the old mapping but should no longer have some caps (e.g., breach)?

zoe: For emergency revoke we support two knobs: 1) per-subject generation increment (instant deny when runtime sees higher gen), 2) global emergency denylist for specific cap identifiers which runtime checks before honoring caps. Keep denylist small and update via pub/sub. Runtime checks are O(1): if cap in denylist -> deny.

harper: Implementation details: mapping blobs are small JSONs (cap -> route set), limited to a few KB. We keep them in a per-region CDN + local memcache. Publish mapping_version changes on an internal event bus with a compact diff (added caps, removed caps). Runtimes subscribe to diffs for hot mappings to pre-warm.

eli: Telemetry: we need mapping_version, token_mapping_version, mapping_fetch_latency, mapping_miss_rate, and mismatch_count (runtime saw token cap not covered by current mapping). Alert on mismatch spikes.

zoe: UX: console shows a preview compare view (v3 vs v2) highlighting added caps. Promote button requires a checklist: audit run >= N calls, zero critical mismatches, and owner approval.

harper: Rollback story: bump mapping_version back and publish a remove-delta. Tokens minted during the faulty window keep their token_mapping_version tag; we can either rotate those tokens (recommended) or enforce a short denylist against the offending caps. Rotation is automated for internal services via the identity broker.

eli: Operational note: keep mapping changes idempotent and include a monotonic version. Use signed mapping manifests so runtimes can verify provenance. Also record the mapping manifest id in mint/audit logs.

zoe: Open questions:
- how large can a mapping blob grow before we need sharding (per-route mapping shards)?
- how do partners view mapping changes when they rely on projected caps?

harper: My suggestions: cap mapping per functional area (ingest, inference, metrics) to bound size. Partners get a notification webhook during promote with preview; require partner opt-in for any mapping that expands their allowed caps.

eli: Action items:
- @harper: prototype mapping_version pub/sub + local memcache + denylist check (ETA 2w)
- @zoe: console preview UI copy + checklist text (ETA 3d)
- @eli: update RFC with emergency revoke primitives and audit linkage (ETA 4d)

audit-bot: Note: mapping promotions will be recorded in audit trail with manifest id and actor.

zoe: dropping a few edge cases (multi-mapping tokens, delegated-transient tokens) in RFC update. Thanks all.
